title: Platformer
summary: How you move and what form you are are two independent questions. A single HSM that combined them ($SmallJumping, $BigFalling, $FieryRunning, …) would explode combinatorially. Frame's answer is orthogonal composition: one orchestrator owns two peer sub-machines — Locomotion (idle/walk/run/jump/fall/land) and PowerUp (small/big/fiery) — and forwards each input to whichever child owns it. Two additive FSMs, not one multiplicative one.
teaches: Orthogonal-state composition vs the matrix-HSM explosion · two independent sibling sub-machines (motion + form) under one orchestrator facade · a child interface call as a handler's return value · push$/pop$ pause that freezes the whole rig
controls: A/D or ←/→ move · Shift/hold run · Space jump (hold = higher) · grab mushroom/flower · P pause · R reset pickups

machines.title: Platformer — the orchestrator facade
machines.blurb: $Playing forwards every input to whichever child owns it (move/jump → loco, pickups → power) and reads their combined state back. take_damage() is the showcase of a child call AS a return value: `@@:(this.power.take_damage())` marshals the PowerUp's bool result back out. pause() is a push$/pop$ that freezes both children at once.

machines.title: Locomotion — how you move
machines.blurb: $Idle → $Walking → $Running, and $Jumping → $Falling → $Landing. $Jumping holds state-local $.jump_held_time (auto-falls at 0.35s unless release_jump freezes it — variable-height jump) and $Landing a $.timer recovery window with a $>() enter handler that clears the pending jump. The scene reads wants_velocity_x()/is_grounded() each frame.

machines.title: PowerUp — what form you are
machines.blurb: $Small → $Big → $Fiery via mushroom/flower, and take_damage() steps back down one form (Fiery→Big→Small), returning whether the hit was absorbed. Fully orthogonal to Locomotion: you can be a running Fiery or an idle Small — the two machines never enumerate each other's states.
